advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the ProviderSession client is closed even when construction/validation between provider build and the run try-block raises (wrap the body in `with ProviderSession(cfg) as session:` or extend the try to cover from build onward).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/runner.py:296: `model = infer_model(resolved, provider_factory=provider_session.provider_factory)`
src/rebar/llm/runner.py:312-313: `if self._model_override is None and tools:` / `_check_tool_capability(model, resolved)` — raises LLMConfigError, and it sits before the try
src/rebar/llm/runner.py:433: `try:` — the block whose finally at line 517-520 calls `provider_session.close()`
ABSENCE: no try/finally or `with ProviderSession(...)` guards the region between line 296 (client opened) and line 433 (try start)
advisory.finding: An exception raised after provider construction but before the try/finally block leaks the opened httpx.AsyncClient. `_check_tool_capability(model, resolved)` (line 313) can raise LLMConfigError, and the model_settings/web-capability assembly (lines 347-394) can also raise, all AFTER `infer_model(... provider_factory=...)` (line 296) has opened and registered a retrying AsyncClient on the session — but `provider_session.close()` only runs in the `finally` of the try that starts at line 433, so on that path the client is never closed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Move provider construction inside the try (or wrap the whole body in `with ProviderSession(cfg) as session:` as the docstring and ticket describe) so close() runs on any post-build exception.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the ProviderSession teardown docstring with the implementation — either adopt the `with` statement in run() or correct the docstring/ticket to describe the finally-based close().
evidence: src/rebar/llm/providers.py:20-23: `the session is a context manager, so ``runner.run()`` wraps its body in ``with ProviderSession(cfg) as session:`` and ``__exit__`` closes everything the builders opened`
src/rebar/llm/runner.py:289: `provider_session = ProviderSession(cfg)` — no `with`
src/rebar/llm/runner.py:517-520: `finally:` / `provider_session.close()` — teardown via finally, not __exit__
src/rebar/llm/providers.py:221-225: `__enter__`/`__exit__` defined but not exercised by run()
advisory.finding: The module docstring (and the ticket plan) claim `runner.run()` wraps its body in `with ProviderSession(cfg) as session:` and relies on `__exit__` for teardown, but the actual implementation constructs the session plainly and calls `provider_session.close()` in a `finally`. The `__enter__`/`__exit__` context-manager methods are therefore dead code in production, and the documentation misrepresents the control flow.
advisory.suggested_fix: Adopt `with ProviderSession(cfg) as provider_session:` in run() (which also closes the leak window), or update the docstring to describe the finally-based teardown.
